resource.name: aws_codebuild_project
resource.description: Provides a CodeBuild Project resource. See also the aws_codebuild_webhook resource, which manages the webhook to the source (e.g., the "rebuild every time a code change is pushed" option in the CodeBuild web console).
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_codebuild_project` resource enables the creation and management of AWS CodeBuild projects, which automate software build and testing workflows in CI/CD pipelines. It supports configurations for source code integration (e.g., Git repositories), build environments, logging, caching, and artifact storage, allowing users to customize build processes for diverse programming languages and frameworks. Common use cases include setting up automated builds triggered by code changes, integrating with version control systems, and optimizing build performance with caching and environment variables.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates the configuration of multiple `aws_codebuild_project` resources, showcasing key features such as integration with GitHub repositories, VPC connectivity, S3 caching, local caching modes, and authentication via CodeStar Connections. It illustrates advanced settings like environment variables, logging configurations, and IAM roles/policies for granular permissions, enabling users to set up CodeBuild projects tailored to diverse build and deployment scenarios.

arguments.name: badge_enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Generates a publicly-accessible URL for the projects build badge. Available as `badge_url` attribute when enabled.
arguments.llm_summary: The `badge_enabled` argument in the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to control whether a publicly accessible URL is generated for the project's build badge, which visually represents the build status. Enabling this feature is useful for integrating build status indicators into external platforms, such as documentation or repositories, to enhance visibility and transparency of project health.

arguments.name: build_timeout
arguments.description: (Optional) Number of minutes, from 5 to 2160 (36 hours), for AWS CodeBuild to wait until timing out any related build that does not get marked as completed. The default is 60 minutes. The `build_timeout` property is not available on the `Lambda` compute type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `build_timeout` argument in the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to define the maximum duration, in minutes (5 to 2160), that AWS CodeBuild will wait for a build to complete before timing out. This configuration helps control build execution limits, ensuring efficient resource usage and preventing stalled builds, but is not applicable for projects using the `Lambda` compute type.

arguments.name: concurrent_build_limit
arguments.description: (Optional) Specify a maximum number of concurrent builds for the project. The value specified must be greater than 0 and less than the account concurrent running builds limit.
arguments.llm_summary: The `concurrent_build_limit` argument for the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to define the maximum number of builds that can run concurrently for a specific CodeBuild project, ensuring controlled resource usage and preventing excessive parallel execution. This configuration is useful for optimizing build workflows, managing account-level concurrency limits, and aligning project build capacity with organizational policies or infrastructure constraints.

arguments.name: description
arguments.description: (Optional) Short description of the project.
arguments.llm_summary: The `description` argument for the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to define a short, human-readable summary of the project's purpose or functionality. This optional metadata helps improve project organization and clarity, especially in environments with multiple CodeBuild projects.

arguments.name: encryption_key
arguments.description: (Optional) AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer master key (CMK) to be used for encrypting the build project's build output artifacts.
arguments.llm_summary: The `encryption_key` argument in the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to specify an AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) for encrypting the build output artifacts of the CodeBuild project. By configuring this argument, users can enhance the security of their build artifacts, ensuring compliance with encryption requirements and protecting sensitive data during and after the build process.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument in the `aws_codebuild_project` resource specifies the unique identifier for the CodeBuild project, allowing users to reference and manage the project within Terraform configurations and other dependent resources. While optional, setting this argument can help ensure consistent identification and tracking of the project across infrastructure workflows.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) Project's name.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument specifies the unique identifier for the CodeBuild project, allowing users to define a meaningful and recognizable name for the project. Setting this argument is essential for organizing and managing build configurations, enabling users to reference and distinguish the project within AWS services and workflows.

arguments.name: project_visibility
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies the visibility of the project's builds. Possible values are: `PUBLIC_READ` and `PRIVATE`. Default value is `PRIVATE`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `project_visibility` argument in the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to define the accessibility of the project's build results, specifying whether they are publicly readable (`PUBLIC_READ`) or restricted to private access (`PRIVATE`). This configuration impacts the visibility of build outputs, aligning with user goals such as controlling access to build artifacts for security or collaboration purposes, with the default setting ensuring private access.

arguments.name: queued_timeout
arguments.description: (Optional) Number of minutes, from 5 to 480 (8 hours), a build is allowed to be queued before it times out. The default is 8 hours. The `queued_timeout` property is not available on the `Lambda` compute type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `queued_timeout` argument for the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to define the maximum time, in minutes (5 to 480), that a build can remain in the queue before timing out. This setting helps control build lifecycle behavior by preventing excessively long queue times, ensuring efficient resource utilization and build pipeline management, but is not applicable when using the `Lambda` compute type.

arguments.name: resource_access_role
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of the IAM role that enables CodeBuild to access the CloudWatch Logs and Amazon S3 artifacts for the project's builds in order to display them publicly. Only applicable if `project_visibility` is `PUBLIC_READ`.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the ARN of an IAM role that grants CodeBuild permissions to access CloudWatch Logs and Amazon S3 artifacts for builds, specifically when the project's visibility is set to `PUBLIC_READ`. Configuring this argument ensures proper access control for publicly visible build outputs and logs, aligning with security and visibility requirements.

arguments.name: service_role
arguments.description: (Required) Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role that enables AWS CodeBuild to interact with dependent AWS services on behalf of the AWS account.
arguments.llm_summary: The `service_role` argument specifies the IAM role (via its ARN) that grants AWS CodeBuild the necessary permissions to interact with other AWS services on behalf of the account. By defining this role, users enable CodeBuild to perform essential operations such as accessing source repositories, storing build artifacts, and managing dependent resources, ensuring secure and seamless integration with the broader AWS ecosystem.

arguments.name: source_version
arguments.description: (Optional) Version of the build input to be built for this project. If not specified, the latest version is used.
arguments.llm_summary: The `source_version` argument in the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to specify the version of the source code to be built, such as a specific branch, tag, or commit in the source repository. By setting this argument, users can control which version of their code is used during the build process, enabling precise builds for testing, deployment, or CI/CD workflows.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) Map of tags to assign to the resource. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to define a map of key-value pairs to assign metadata tags to the CodeBuild project. This enables resource organization, cost allocation, and searchability by categorizing the project with labels such as environment, team, or purpose. If provider-level `default_tags` are configured, this argument allows overriding those tags for more granular control.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are automatically propagated to all resources associated with the CodeBuild project. This enables streamlined resource organization, cost allocation, and metadata management, aligning with common user goals like tagging for governance, billing, and searchability across AWS services.

blocks.name: artifacts

arguments.name: artifact_identifier
arguments.description: (Optional) Artifact identifier. Must be the same specified inside the AWS CodeBuild build specification.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines a unique identifier for the build artifact within the AWS CodeBuild project, ensuring alignment with the artifact configuration specified in the build specification file. This argument allows users to explicitly reference and manage specific artifacts during the build process, supporting workflows that require precise artifact tracking or differentiation.

arguments.name: bucket_owner_access
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies the bucket owner's access for objects that another account uploads to their Amazon S3 bucket. By default, only the account that uploads the objects to the bucket has access to these objects. This property allows you to give the bucket owner access to these objects. Valid values are `NONE`, `READ_ONLY`, and `FULL`. your CodeBuild service role must have the `s3:PutBucketAcl` permission. This permission allows CodeBuild to modify the access control list for the bucket.
arguments.llm_summary: The `bucket_owner_access` argument in the `artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to specify the level of access granted to the Amazon S3 bucket owner for objects uploaded by CodeBuild. By setting this property (`NONE`, `READ_ONLY`, or `FULL`), users can control the bucket owner's permissions for these artifacts, ensuring compliance with access control requirements and enabling collaboration or ownership management for cross-account S3 buckets.

arguments.name: encryption_disabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to disable encrypting output artifacts. If `type` is set to `NO_ARTIFACTS`, this value is ignored. Defaults to `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `encryption_disabled` argument in the `artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to control whether output artifacts are encrypted. Setting this to `true` disables encryption, which may be useful for simplifying artifact handling in non-sensitive workflows, but is ignored if `type` is set to `NO_ARTIFACTS`.

arguments.name: location
arguments.description: (Optional) Information about the build output artifact location. If `type` is set to `CODEPIPELINE` or `NO_ARTIFACTS`, this value is ignored. If `type` is set to `S3`, this is the name of the output bucket.
arguments.llm_summary: The `location` argument in the `artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource specifies the name of the S3 bucket where build output artifacts are stored when the artifact `type` is set to `S3`. This allows users to define the storage destination for build outputs, enabling integration with S3 for artifact management and retrieval.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Optional) Name of the project. If `type` is set to `S3`, this is the name of the output artifact object
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument in the `artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to specify the name of the output artifact object when the artifact `type` is set to `S3`. This enables users to define a custom identifier for the artifact stored in the S3 bucket, supporting better organization and retrieval of build outputs in cloud storage.

arguments.name: namespace_type
arguments.description: (Optional) Namespace to use in storing build artifacts. If `type` is set to `S3`, then valid values are `BUILD_ID`, `NONE`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `namespace_type` argument in the `artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to define how build artifacts are organized within an S3 bucket. By specifying `BUILD_ID`, artifacts are stored in a unique namespace tied to the build ID, enabling traceability and isolation for individual builds, while `NONE` disables namespace creation, storing artifacts directly in the specified bucket path. This configuration helps users control artifact storage structure to align with their build management and retention strategies.

arguments.name: override_artifact_name
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether a name specified in the build specification overrides the artifact name.
arguments.llm_summary: The `override_artifact_name` argument in the `artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to control whether the artifact name defined in the build specification file takes precedence over the default artifact name configured in the project. Setting this to `true` enables dynamic artifact naming based on the build specification, which is useful for customizing artifact outputs to align with specific build or deployment workflows.

arguments.name: packaging
arguments.description: (Optional) Type of build output artifact to create. If `type` is set to `S3`, valid values are `NONE`, `ZIP`
arguments.llm_summary: The `packaging` argument in the `artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to specify the format of the build output artifact when the artifact type is set to `S3`. By setting this argument to either `NONE` or `ZIP`, users can control whether the output is stored as individual files or compressed into a single ZIP archive, enabling customization of artifact storage and retrieval based on project requirements.

arguments.name: path
arguments.description: (Optional) If `type` is set to `S3`, this is the path to the output artifact.
arguments.llm_summary: The `path` argument in the `artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to specify the S3 path where the output artifacts from the CodeBuild project will be stored. By defining this path, users can control the organization and location of build outputs in their S3 bucket, enabling structured artifact management and facilitating retrieval or integration with downstream workflows.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: (Required) Build output artifact's type. Valid values: `CODEPIPELINE`, `NO_ARTIFACTS`, `S3`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument in the `artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource specifies the output artifact's storage and delivery method, allowing users to define how build results are handled. By setting this required argument to one of the valid values (`CODEPIPELINE`, `NO_ARTIFACTS`, or `S3`), users can configure whether artifacts are integrated with AWS CodePipeline, omitted entirely, or stored in an S3 bucket, aligning the build process with their deployment or storage strategy.

blocks.llm_summary: The `artifacts` configuration block in the `aws_codebuild_project` resource defines how build output artifacts are managed, including their type, location, encryption, and packaging. This block enables users to specify where and how build results are stored, ensuring proper delivery and accessibility of build outputs, such as archives or files, to downstream processes or storage systems.

blocks.name: build_batch_config
blocks.description: (Optional) Defines the batch build options for the project.

arguments.name: combine_artifacts
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies if the build artifacts for the batch build should be combined into a single artifact location.
arguments.llm_summary: The `combine_artifacts` argument in the `build_batch_config` of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to control whether the artifacts generated by individual builds in a batch are merged into a single artifact location. Setting this to `true` simplifies artifact management by consolidating outputs, which is useful for workflows requiring unified build results, such as packaging or deployment pipelines.

arguments.name: service_role
arguments.description: (Required) Specifies the service role ARN for the batch build project.
arguments.llm_summary: The `service_role` argument in the `build_batch_config` of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource specifies the IAM role ARN that grants permissions for CodeBuild to execute batch builds. By defining this required role, users ensure the batch build process can access necessary AWS resources, such as source repositories, artifacts, and logs, aligning with security and operational requirements.

arguments.name: timeout_in_mins
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies the maximum amount of time, in minutes, that the batch build must be completed in.
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the maximum duration, in minutes, for completing a batch build within the `build_batch_config` of an `aws_codebuild_project`, allowing users to control build execution time limits to prevent prolonged or stalled batch processes and align with project time constraints or resource optimization goals."

blocks.name: restrictions
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block specifying the restrictions for the batch build. Detailed below.

arguments.name: compute_types_allowed
arguments.description: (Optional) An array of strings that specify the compute types that are allowed for the batch build. See Build environment compute types in the AWS CodeBuild User Guide for these values.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines a list of allowed compute types for batch builds within the AWS CodeBuild project, enabling users to restrict the build environment to specific instance types for resource optimization or compliance purposes. This argument helps control the scalability and cost-efficiency of the build process by specifying which compute resources can be utilized.

arguments.name: maximum_builds_allowed
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies the maximum number of builds allowed.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the maximum number of concurrent builds permitted for the CodeBuild project, allowing users to control resource utilization and enforce limits on build execution. This argument helps manage project scalability and prevent overconsumption of build resources, aligning with operational or cost management goals.

blocks.llm_summary: The "restrictions" configuration block within the "build_batch_config" of the "aws_codebuild_project" resource defines constraints for batch builds, such as limiting resource usage or controlling execution parameters. It enables users to enforce specific rules or boundaries for batch build operations, ensuring compliance with organizational policies or optimizing resource allocation.

The `build_batch_config` block in the `aws_codebuild_project` resource defines batch build settings, enabling the execution of multiple builds concurrently as part of a batch process. It encapsulates options such as batch build behavior, dependencies, and configurations, allowing users to optimize build workflows for parallel execution and manage complex build pipelines efficiently.

blocks.name: cache

arguments.name: location
arguments.description: (Required when cache type is `S3`) Location where the AWS CodeBuild project stores cached resources. For type `S3`, the value must be a valid S3 bucket name/prefix.
arguments.llm_summary: The `location` argument for the `aws_codebuild_project` resource's `cache` block specifies the S3 bucket and optional prefix where cached build resources are stored when the cache type is set to `S3`. Configuring this argument enables users to define the storage location for reusable build artifacts, optimizing build performance and reducing redundant resource downloads.

arguments.name: modes
arguments.description: (Required when cache type is `LOCAL`) Specifies settings that AWS CodeBuild uses to store and reuse build dependencies. Valid values: `LOCAL_SOURCE_CACHE`, `LOCAL_DOCKER_LAYER_CACHE`, `LOCAL_CUSTOM_CACHE`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `modes` argument for the `cache` configuration in the `aws_codebuild_project` resource specifies the caching strategies AWS CodeBuild uses to optimize build performance by storing and reusing build dependencies. By defining valid modes such as `LOCAL_SOURCE_CACHE`, `LOCAL_DOCKER_LAYER_CACHE`, or `LOCAL_CUSTOM_CACHE`, users can control how build artifacts, Docker layers, or custom data are cached locally, reducing build times and improving resource efficiency.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: (Optional) Type of storage that will be used for the AWS CodeBuild project cache. Valid values: `NO_CACHE`, `LOCAL`, `S3`. Defaults to `NO_CACHE`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument in the `cache` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource specifies the storage mechanism for the build cache, allowing users to define whether caching is disabled (`NO_CACHE`), uses local ephemeral storage (`LOCAL`), or leverages an S3 bucket (`S3`). Configuring this argument impacts build performance and cost optimization by enabling or customizing caching behavior to reduce build times and resource usage.

blocks.llm_summary: The `cache` configuration block in the `aws_codebuild_project` resource defines caching mechanisms to optimize build performance by storing reusable build artifacts, such as dependencies or intermediate files. It encapsulates settings for cache type (e.g., S3 or local) and location, enabling users to reduce build times and improve efficiency by reusing data across builds.

blocks.name: environment

arguments.name: certificate
arguments.description: (Optional) ARN of the S3 bucket, path prefix and object key that contains the PEM-encoded certificate.
arguments.llm_summary: The `certificate` argument in the `environment` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to specify the ARN of an S3 object containing a PEM-encoded certificate. This certificate is used to configure secure connections or authentication mechanisms within the build environment, enabling enhanced security for build processes that require trusted certificates.

arguments.name: compute_type
arguments.description: (Required) Information about the compute resources the build project will use. Valid values: `BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL`, `BUILD_GENERAL1_MEDIUM`, `BUILD_GENERAL1_LARGE`, `BUILD_GENERAL1_2XLARGE`, `BUILD_LAMBDA_1GB`, `BUILD_LAMBDA_2GB`, `BUILD_LAMBDA_4GB`, `BUILD_LAMBDA_8GB`, `BUILD_LAMBDA_10GB`. `BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL` is only valid if `type` is set to `LINUX_CONTAINER`. When `type` is set to `LINUX_GPU_CONTAINER`, `compute_type` must be `BUILD_GENERAL1_LARGE`. When `type` is set to `LINUX_LAMBDA_CONTAINER` or `ARM_LAMBDA_CONTAINER`, `compute_type` must be `BUILD_LAMBDA_XGB`.`
arguments.llm_summary: The `compute_type` argument specifies the type and size of compute resources allocated for the build environment in an AWS CodeBuild project, directly impacting the performance and cost of build operations. It allows users to tailor the environment to their workload requirements, such as selecting general-purpose, GPU-optimized, or Lambda-based compute types, ensuring compatibility with the build environment's `type` and optimizing resource utilization for tasks like containerized builds or serverless workflows.

arguments.name: image
arguments.description: (Required) Docker image to use for this build project. Valid values include Docker images provided by CodeBuild ( e.g `aws/codebuild/amazonlinux2-x86_64-standard:4.0`), Docker Hub images (e.g., `hashicorp/terraform:latest`), and full Docker repository URIs such as those for ECR (e.g., `137112412989.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/amazonlinux:latest`).
arguments.llm_summary: The `image` argument specifies the Docker image used to define the runtime environment for the build process in an AWS CodeBuild project. By setting this required parameter, users control the software stack and dependencies available during the build, enabling compatibility with specific tools, frameworks, or operating systems necessary for their CI/CD workflows.

arguments.name: image_pull_credentials_type
arguments.description: (Optional) Type of credentials AWS CodeBuild uses to pull images in your build. Valid values: `CODEBUILD`, `SERVICE_ROLE`. When you use a cross-account or private registry image, you must use SERVICE_ROLE credentials. When you use an AWS CodeBuild curated image, you must use CodeBuild credentials. Defaults to `CODEBUILD`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `image_pull_credentials_type` argument specifies the type of credentials AWS CodeBuild uses to authenticate when pulling container images for the build environment. It allows users to control whether CodeBuild uses its own managed credentials (`CODEBUILD`) or credentials tied to a service role (`SERVICE_ROLE`), which is required for cross-account or private registry images. This configuration ensures proper access management for image sources, aligning with user goals like securing build environments and enabling private or external image usage.

arguments.name: privileged_mode
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to enable running the Docker daemon inside a Docker container. Defaults to `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `privileged_mode` argument in the `environment` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to control whether the Docker daemon can run inside a Docker container during build execution. Enabling this functionality (`true`) is typically required for builds that involve Docker-in-Docker workflows, such as building or testing container images, providing enhanced flexibility for containerized CI/CD pipelines.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: (Required) Type of build environment to use for related builds. Valid values: `LINUX_CONTAINER`, `LINUX_GPU_CONTAINER`, `WINDOWS_CONTAINER` (deprecated), `WINDOWS_SERVER_2019_CONTAINER`, `ARM_CONTAINER`, `LINUX_LAMBDA_CONTAINER`, `ARM_LAMBDA_CONTAINER`. For additional information, see the CodeBuild User Guide.
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument specifies the build environment's underlying platform and runtime configuration for the `aws_codebuild_project`, allowing users to define the operating system, container type, and architecture used during builds. Setting this argument ensures compatibility with specific workloads, such as Linux, Windows, GPU-based, ARM-based, or Lambda-based builds, aligning the environment with the project's requirements and execution goals.

blocks.name: environment_variable

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) Environment variable's name or key.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument specifies the unique identifier or key for an environment variable within an AWS CodeBuild project's build environment. By defining this required string, users can configure custom environment variables to pass dynamic values, secrets, or configuration data into the build process, enabling tailored build behavior and automation.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: (Optional) Type of environment variable. Valid values: `PARAMETER_STORE`, `PLAINTEXT`, `SECRETS_MANAGER`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument for the `environment_variable` in the `aws_codebuild_project` resource specifies the source of the environment variable, allowing users to define whether the variable is plaintext (`PLAINTEXT`), retrieved securely from AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store (`PARAMETER_STORE`), or managed via AWS Secrets Manager (`SECRETS_MANAGER`). This enables users to control how sensitive data or configuration values are stored and accessed during CodeBuild project execution, aligning with security and operational requirements.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: (Required) Environment variable's value.
arguments.llm_summary: The `value` argument specifies the actual content or data assigned to an environment variable in the `aws_codebuild_project` resource, enabling users to define dynamic configuration values such as credentials, paths, or runtime settings for CodeBuild build environments. By setting this argument, users can control the behavior of their build processes and ensure the necessary variables are available during execution.

blocks.llm_summary: The `environment_variable` configuration block within the `environment` context of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource defines key-value pairs for custom environment variables used during the build process. This block enables users to inject dynamic or static values into the build environment, facilitating customization of build behavior, integration with external systems, or secure handling of sensitive data like API keys and credentials.

blocks.name: fleet

arguments.name: fleet_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) Compute fleet ARN for the build project.
arguments.llm_summary: The `fleet_arn` argument for the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a compute fleet to be associated with the build project. By setting this argument, users can define the fleet that provides the underlying compute resources for build execution, enabling customized resource allocation and scaling for build processes.

blocks.llm_summary: The "fleet" configuration block within the "environment" context of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource is used to define and manage settings related to the compute fleet used for build execution. It encapsulates parameters that control the type, size, and provisioning of the underlying compute resources, enabling users to optimize build performance and resource allocation for their CodeBuild projects. Configuring this block allows for tailored compute environments that align with specific build requirements, such as scaling or specialized hardware needs.

blocks.name: registry_credential

arguments.name: credential
arguments.description: (Required) ARN or name of credentials created using AWS Secrets Manager.
arguments.llm_summary: The `credential` argument specifies the ARN or name of credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager, enabling the CodeBuild project to authenticate with a private Docker registry. By configuring this required parameter, users can securely manage access to container images during the build process, aligning with common goals like setting up secure environment dependencies and integrating private registries.

arguments.name: credential_provider
arguments.description: (Required) Service that created the credentials to access a private Docker registry. Valid value: `SECRETS_MANAGER` (AWS Secrets Manager).
arguments.llm_summary: The `credential_provider` argument specifies the service responsible for managing credentials used to authenticate with a private Docker registry in the `registry_credential` configuration of an `aws_codebuild_project`. By setting this required argument to `SECRETS_MANAGER`, users enable secure integration with AWS Secrets Manager, ensuring sensitive registry credentials are retrieved and managed securely during the build process.

blocks.llm_summary: The `registry_credential` block within the `environment` configuration of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource defines authentication details for accessing private container image registries. It encapsulates settings such as credential type and the ARN of the secret storing the credentials, enabling secure integration with private registries to pull container images during the build process. Configuring this block ensures seamless and secure access to private images, supporting advanced build workflows in CodeBuild.

The "environment" configuration block in the "aws_codebuild_project" resource defines the runtime environment for CodeBuild projects, including compute type, image, and environment variables. It enables users to specify build settings such as the operating system, programming language runtime, and custom configurations, ensuring the build process runs in a tailored and controlled environment.

blocks.name: file_system_locations
blocks.description: (Optional) A set of file system locations to mount inside the build. File system locations are documented below.

arguments.name: identifier
arguments.description: (Optional) The name used to access a file system created by Amazon EFS. CodeBuild creates an environment variable by appending the identifier in all capital letters to CODEBUILD_. For example, if you specify my-efs for identifier, a new environment variable is create named CODEBUILD_MY-EFS.
arguments.llm_summary: The `identifier` argument in the `file_system_locations` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to define a custom name for accessing an Amazon EFS file system within the CodeBuild environment. This name is used to automatically create an environment variable (`CODEBUILD_<IDENTIFIER>`) that simplifies referencing the file system during build processes, enabling streamlined integration with EFS for tasks like caching or file storage.

arguments.name: location
arguments.description: (Optional) A string that specifies the location of the file system created by Amazon EFS. Its format is `efs-dns-name:/directory-path`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `location` argument in the `file_system_locations` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to specify the Amazon EFS file system's DNS name and directory path (`efs-dns-name:/directory-path`) to be mounted during the build process. Configuring this argument enables CodeBuild to access and utilize persistent storage for build artifacts, dependencies, or caching, supporting workflows that require shared or durable file system access.

arguments.name: mount_options
arguments.description: (Optional) The mount options for a file system created by AWS EFS.
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines custom mount options for an AWS EFS file system used in CodeBuild, allowing users to control file system behavior such as access permissions, caching, or performance settings during build execution."

arguments.name: mount_point
arguments.description: (Optional) The location in the container where you mount the file system.
arguments.llm_summary: The `mount_point` argument in the `file_system_locations` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource specifies the directory path within the build container where the associated file system will be mounted. Configuring this argument allows users to define the container's access point for file system storage, enabling seamless integration of external file systems for build processes, such as caching, artifact storage, or shared data access.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: (Optional) The type of the file system. The one supported type is `EFS`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument in the `file_system_locations` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource specifies the type of file system to be used for the CodeBuild project, with the supported option being `EFS` (Elastic File System). This allows users to define the file system integration for their build environment, enabling persistent storage for build artifacts or shared data across build processes.

arguments.name: bucket_owner_access
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies the bucket owner's access for objects that another account uploads to their Amazon S3 bucket. arguments.name: status

arguments.name: bucket_owner_access
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies the bucket owner's access for objects that another account uploads to their Amazon S3 bucket. Valid values are `NONE`, `READ_ONLY`, and `FULL`. The CodeBuild service role must have the `s3:PutBucketAcl` permission. arguments.llm_summary: The `bucket_owner_access` argument in the `secondary_artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to define the level of access granted to the owner of an Amazon S3 bucket for objects uploaded by CodeBuild. By specifying values like `NONE`, `READ_ONLY`, or `FULL`, users can control object permissions to align with cross-account access requirements, ensuring proper collaboration or compliance while leveraging the CodeBuild service role's `s3:PutBucketAcl` permission.

arguments.name: encryption_disabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to disable encrypting output artifacts. If `type` is set to `NO_ARTIFACTS`, this value is ignored. Defaults to `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `encryption_disabled` argument in the `secondary_artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to control whether output artifacts are encrypted during storage. Setting this to `true` disables encryption, which may be useful for simplifying artifact handling in non-sensitive workflows, while leaving it as `false` (default) ensures artifacts are securely encrypted. This argument is ignored if the artifact type is set to `NO_ARTIFACTS`.

arguments.name: location
arguments.description: (Optional) Information about the build output artifact location. If `type` is set to `CODEPIPELINE` or `NO_ARTIFACTS`, this value is ignored if specified. If `type` is set to `S3`, this is the name of the output bucket. If `path` is not specified, `location` can specify the path of the output artifact in the output bucket.
arguments.llm_summary: The `location` argument in the `secondary_artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource specifies the storage destination for build output artifacts when the artifact `type` is set to `S3`. It allows users to define the name of the S3 bucket and optionally the path within the bucket where the artifacts will be stored, enabling precise control over artifact organization and retrieval. This argument is ignored for artifact types `CODEPIPELINE` or `NO_ARTIFACTS`.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Optional) Name of the project. If `type` is set to `CODEPIPELINE` or `NO_ARTIFACTS`, this value is ignored if specified. If `type` is set to `S3`, this is the name of the output artifact object.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the name of the output artifact object for a secondary artifact when the `type` is set to `S3`, allowing users to specify a unique identifier for the artifact in the S3 bucket. arguments.name: namespace_type
arguments.description: (Optional) Namespace to use in storing build artifacts. If `type` is set to `CODEPIPELINE` or `NO_ARTIFACTS`, this value is ignored if specified. If `type` is set to `S3`, valid values are `BUILD_ID` or `NONE`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `namespace_type` argument in the `secondary_artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource specifies how build artifacts are organized within an S3 bucket when the artifact `type` is set to `S3`. It allows users to control whether artifacts are stored under a unique build-specific namespace (`BUILD_ID`) or without any namespace (`NONE`), enabling better organization or simplified access depending on the user's artifact management strategy.

arguments.name: override_artifact_name
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether a name specified in the build specification overrides the artifact name.
arguments.llm_summary: The `override_artifact_name` argument in the `secondary_artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to control whether the artifact name specified in the build specification takes precedence over the default artifact name defined in the project configuration. Setting this to `true` enables dynamic artifact naming based on the build specification, which is useful for customizing artifact outputs in scenarios like versioning or environment-specific builds.

arguments.name: packaging
arguments.description: (Optional) Type of build output artifact to create. If `type` is set to `CODEPIPELINE` or `NO_ARTIFACTS`, this value is ignored if specified. If `type` is set to `S3`, valid values are `NONE` or `ZIP`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `packaging` argument in the `secondary_artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource specifies the format of the build output artifact when the artifact type is set to `S3`, allowing users to control whether the output is stored as a plain file (`NONE`) or compressed into a ZIP archive (`ZIP`). This configuration is ignored for artifact types `CODEPIPELINE` or `NO_ARTIFACTS` and is typically used to define how build outputs are packaged for storage or distribution in S3.

arguments.name: path
arguments.description: (Optional) Along with `namespace_type` and `name`, the pattern that AWS CodeBuild uses to name and store the output artifact. If `type` is set to `CODEPIPELINE` or `NO_ARTIFACTS`, this value is ignored if specified. If `type` is set to `S3`, this is the path to the output artifact.
arguments.llm_summary: The `path` argument in the `secondary_artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource allows users to define the storage path for output artifacts when the artifact type is set to `S3`. This configuration helps control the organization and naming structure of build outputs, enabling users to specify where artifacts are stored within the S3 bucket for better management and retrieval.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: (Required) Build output artifact's type. Valid values `CODEPIPELINE`, `NO_ARTIFACTS`, and `S3`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument in the `secondary_artifacts` block of the `aws_codebuild_project` resource specifies the output artifact's storage destination or integration method, allowing users to define whether the build outputs are sent to an S3 bucket, integrated with AWS CodePipeline, or omitted entirely (`NO_ARTIFACTS`). This configuration is essential for controlling how and where secondary build artifacts are stored or utilized, aligning with common goals like enabling CI/CD workflows or managing artifact storage.

blocks.llm_summary: The `secondary_artifacts` configuration block in the `aws_codebuild_project` resource defines additional output artifacts generated by a CodeBuild project, enabling users to specify multiple artifact destinations or formats beyond the primary artifact. This block encapsulates settings related to artifact type, location, encryption, and packaging, allowing users to manage complex build workflows that produce multiple outputs for deployment, storage, or further processing.

blocks.name: secondary_source_version

arguments.name: source_identifier
